notes: Access: us.hay.com 301-redirects to DWR (retailer); the genuine HAY-owned catalogue is www.hay.com (confirmed by prior Furniture pass notes at notes/26.md; re-verified live, direct HTTP fetch works, no block). Checked robots.txt: general User-agent Allow:/, only specific bot UAs (Amazonbot, Applebot-Extended, Bytespider, CCBot, ClaudeBot, CloudflareBrowserRenderingCrawler, Google-Extended, GPTBot, meta-externalagent) are disallowed - this governs crawler/AI-training bots, not a direct-fetch/interactive-browse block, and tier-1 direct HTTP fetch was used throughout (no Claude-in-Chrome needed). Navigation discovery: full main nav mega-menu for Products (Furniture / Lighting / Accessories) captured from homepage HTML. Found genuine site-defined 'New' nav entries labelled 'New Furniture', 'New Lighting', 'New Accessories' at /products/furniture/new, /products/lighting/new, /products/accessories/new - these are real PLPs (div.hayproduct product-tile markup identical to every other verified category PLP in the prior Furniture pass), each confirmed via <title> tag: 'New furniture collection - see the latest designs from HAY', 'New design products just launched from HAY', 'New accessories - enjoy the latest designs from HAY'. Applied the Collection-page test: opened each page and confirmed it is a real browsable product grid (not editorial/campaign copy) - passes. Also checked footer nav, sitemap-index (hay.com/sitemaps/sitemap-index.xml -> sitemap-content.xml, sitemap-products.xml, sitemap-variants.xml), and site search (Playwright, terms 'new arrivals') - search UI returned no distinct results panel (client-rendered widget, inconclusive) but nav+sitemap evidence is sufficient and consistent. No other New Arrivals/New In/Just Launched pages found outside these three section-specific ones; no unified single New Arrivals URL exists (each product vertical has its own). qty methodology: same as prior Furniture pass for this company - HAY publishes no 'N items' header anywhere on www.hay.com; each PLP embeds pagingSettings with pagingEnabled:false, showCount:0, meaning the full product set is server-rendered in the initial HTML with no lazy pagination, so qty = exhaustive count of div.hayproduct nodes (verified via direct grep of the fetched HTML). New Furniture's page additionally contains a 'Line Extensions' sub-heading partway down (2 of the 28 tiles) for new colour/material variants of existing products, on the same URL/page as the primary 'New' items (26 tiles) - no separate URL exists to split them, so the full page total (28) is reported as this PLP's qty; this nuance is recorded in the row's evidence field.
